introduction: Today the Church commemorates all the faithful departed. We pray for all who have died, especially our own loved ones, that they may be purified and come into the light of God's presence. Isaiah promises that God will destroy death forever and wipe away the tears from every face. Paul proclaims that Christ has been raised, the first fruits of those who have fallen asleep. Let us pray for the dead with hope.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of all who sleep. With faith and hope, let us pray for all the faithful departed.
intentions: For all the faithful departed, especially those we have known and loved: that God may bring them into his light and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who died alone, suddenly or forgotten, and for whom no one prays: that the Lord may welcome them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who grieve: that the Lord may wipe away their tears and strengthen their hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the dying: that they may meet the Lord in peace, with the help of the sacraments. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live each day ready to meet the Lord, and that we may one day be reunited with those we love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of the living and the dead, your Son conquered death and opened for us the gates of life. Grant to all the faithful departed a place of rest, light and peace, and bring us one day to share their joy. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: He has swallowed up death forever
reflection.body:
On the day after All Saints, the Church turns to all who have died and prays for them. We believe that many who die in God's friendship still need to be purified before they enter fully into his presence, and that our prayers, and above all the Mass offered for them, can help them. This is one of the most human and most Christian things we do: we do not forget our dead.

Isaiah gives us a picture of what God has prepared. On his holy mountain he will hold a feast for all peoples. "He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces." And the people will say, "Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us!"

Paul tells us why we can believe this. Some in Corinth doubted the resurrection, and he answers them: "If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain." But Christ has been raised: "But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep." And "as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive." The last enemy, death itself, will be destroyed.

The psalm that many people ask for at funerals expresses our trust: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me."

In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples that following him means taking up the cross, and that "whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it." Death, for those who belong to Christ, is not the end but a passage.

Today, pray by name for those you have lost. Visit a grave if you can, or light a candle. Have a Mass offered for someone who has died. And thank God for the hope that we will meet again.
